resources.string: If a site breaks, write its domain here, one per line: it and every name under it are never blocked.
Names on a public ad and tracker list get no answer, in every app. The list is fetched through Shroudly and refreshed weekly.
Every app on this device goes through Shroudly.
Battery settings can stop Shroudly in the background and cut your connection. Let it run without battery restrictions.
No internet: Shroudly cannot get through on this network right now, and Android is set to block connections without a VPN. Shroudly keeps trying.
The new mode is used the next time protection starts.

Shroudly runs as a proxy on 127.0.0.1:{port} (SOCKS5 and HTTP) and leaves the VPN to another app. Only apps set to use it go through Shroudly: the Wi-Fi network\'s proxy (host 127.0.0.1, port {port}) or an app\'s own proxy setting.
Every app goes through Shroudly. Android allows one VPN at a time, so another VPN app is disconnected.
Protection stopped because Shroudly could not reach the internet on this network, so your apps are connecting directly. Open Shroudly to try again.
Protection stopped because of an error, so your apps are connecting directly. Open Shroudly to start it again.
Proxy only: apps set to use 127.0.0.1:{port} go through Shroudly
Protection comes on by itself after the phone restarts, once the VPN has been allowed.
Shroudly needs the VPN permission to carry your apps\' connections.
Protection was switched off by Android, usually because another VPN app was turned on.
This network stops {app}\'s connections, and none of Shroudly\'s techniques got through. Use {app}\'s own proxy setting or a VPN.
{app} cannot reach its servers: this network blocks their addresses, and Shroudly cannot get around that without a server elsewhere. Use {app}\'s own proxy setting or a VPN.
Their traffic goes straight out, past Shroudly: for example a game that does not need it.
Shroudly is free and open source under the MIT license: anyone can read, audit and build its code.
Count me in the live total

Sends a random number that changes every launch, so the app can show how many copies are running. It is only sent while protection is on, so it travels the same protected path as the rest of your traffic. Turn it off if you would rather your network saw nothing from Shroudly at all.
Start protection to see live traffic.
